**The 1891 round - Cavendish Crescent South, Lenton Road and the whole of Park Valley.** RG12/2682, transcribed by A. Hagues. **Read to close the 1891 holes**, which [[every-census-gap-and-where-to-start]] now puts ahead of everything else.

**Nine holes closed outright**, each a house the record held in 1881 and again in 1901 or 1911 but not in between:

| schedule | house | who |
|---|---|---|
| 170 | **25 Lenton Road** | Hannah Maria Hopkins, her brother and two sisters - the household [[every-census-gap-and-where-to-start]] named as one of the six with the same family on both sides |
| 171a | **29 Lenton Road** | Frederick Carver, lace manufacturer |
| 172 | **31 Lenton Road** | Henry Clarke, lace manufacturer, at 48 in 1881 and 58 here |
| 174 | **Cliff House** | George Parr, solicitor, with **eight children, two nieces and five servants** - seventeen in the house |
| 175 | **Rock House, 37 Lenton Road** | Charles Shaw, 75, living on own means, who was 65 here in 1881 |
| 64 | **21 Cavendish Crescent South** | Mary Ann Allen, 80, and her daughter Sarah, 53 - the second of the six named as having the same family either side. Richard Allen the bookseller has died |
| 65 | **19 Cavendish Crescent South** | Alfred Page, haberdasher |
| 66 | **17 Cavendish Crescent South** | Kate Green, 27, keeping house for nobody but two servants |
| 67 | **15 Cavendish Crescent South** | Maria Bell, widow, 38, with five children |

**Schedule 63 is 23 Cavendish Crescent South** - Holroyd House, where James Cloak the grocer was in 1881 at 67 and is here at 76, with six grown children still at home. That house already held 1891, so this only fills it out.

**The numbers at the top of the page are hard to read** - 25, 27 and 29 could each be taken for 75, 77 and 79. They are settled by the households themselves: the Hopkins are at 25 in 1881 and 1901, Samuel Waite Johnson is at Lenton House, 27, in every other round, and the run is continuous.

**Three households on these pages are deliberately left out**, because the record already holds them for 1891: Samuel Waite Johnson at **Lenton House (27 Lenton Road)**, James Bennett Gayton at **1 Holles Crescent**, and William Barrett at **1 Park Drive**.

**One cannot be filed.** Schedule 180 gives **5 Park Drive** and the record has no number 5 - Park Drive runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9. The household is Margaret King Allen, widow, whom the 1881 round puts at **3** Park Drive with the same daughter ten years younger. Left for now rather than moved on a guess.

**Joseph Newbold the coachman** carries a street and no number, so he is unfiled. He was a coachman in The Park in 1871 too, in John Adams's household.

---

## A second enumeration district, schedules 146 to 170

**These pages are a different district of the same book**, not a continuation. Both runs number their schedules 146 upwards, and both are internally sequential and continuous, so the numbers cannot be one series: 159 is William Martin at 11 Lenton Road on one run and Benjamin North on Cavendish Road East on the other. Every source line now names its district, because the schedule number alone no longer identifies a household in this file. See [[two-schedule-series-in-rg12-2682]].

**Five houses filled out**, none of them a hole the gap list had open, but all of them thin or empty in the record: **1 Tattershall Drive** (William Henry Truman, wine merchant), **Ashley House on Park Drive** (Alfred Cleaver, lace dresser), **Overdale on Cavendish Road East** (Edward Hardy, retired grocer), **Charnwood, 10 Cavendish Crescent North** (Frederick Wm Goddard - the record held one person here for 1891 and this gives nine) and **Ellington House, Tattershall Drive** (Richard B Brindley, Congregational minister).

### The Cavendish Road East run turns onto Cavendish Crescent North at schedule 161

**Settled, and not by guessing.** Schedules 153 to 164 are written under **Cavendish R<sup>d</sup> East**, the street given once and then carried down the column as ditto marks. It is wrong for the back half of the run, and the 1894 street directory - three years after the census - gives the street for eight of the twelve households outright:

| schedule | household | 1894 directory | street |
|---|---|---|---|
| 153 | Edward Hardy | *Overdale, Mr. Edward Hardy* | Cavendish Road East |
| 154 | Charles Sudbury | *Cavendish house, Charles Sudbury, of C. & F. Sudbury* | Cavendish Road East |
| 155 | Bertha Lloyd at Castle Dene | *Castle Dene* | Cavendish Road East |
| 157 | Robert Hy Speed | *R. H. Speed, solicitor* | Cavendish Road East |
| 158 | Parker Woodward | *Parker Woodward, solicitor* | Cavendish Road East |
| 159 | Benjamin North | *Allandale, Bjn. North, whlsl drgst* | Cavendish Road East |
| 161 | James Smith | *Crescent lodge, James Smith, of E. Smith & Sons* | **Cavendish Crescent North** |
| 163 | Thomas Page | *Hazlewood, Thomas Page, firm of Jonathan Page* | **Cavendish Crescent North** |
| 164 | Frederick Wm Goddard | *Frederick Wm. Goddard, lace mfr* | **Cavendish Crescent North** |

**The turn is at schedule 160**, which is the one household in the run the enumerator did *not* ditto - Charles Loder the coachman, written plainly under **Huntingdon Drive**. He crossed the end of Cavendish Road East, took the Huntingdon Drive cottage, came onto the crescent and went on dittoing the street he had left behind.

**And the house names close it.** The property record already holds **Charnwood as 10 Cavendish Crescent North** and **Hazlewood as 12** - from a walk of the crescent and from the house's own listed-building description, neither of which came from a census. Goddard is at Charnwood in schedule 164 and Page at Hazlewood in 163. Read with Fraser at 162, the enumerator walks the crescent **downwards - Crescent Lodge, 14, 12, 10** - and the 1894 directory prints the same three houses in the opposite order, which is what a directory does.

**Four houses filed on this.** Schedule 154 to **Cavendish House** (#56), 159 to **Allandale, 23 Cavendish Road East** (#50), 162 to **14 Cavendish Crescent North** (#29) - where the record already had this household, so the record was right and the page was wrong - and 163 to **Hazlewood, 12 Cavendish Crescent North** (#28), the pivot that house had been waiting for.

**Still unfiled, but the street is now certain rather than suspect**: Castle Dene and Crescent Lodge, which the property list has not got, and the four households the page gives no number or house name for at all. See [[the-cavendish-road-east-ditto-run]].

**Two uninhabited houses are on these pages** - one on Tattershall Drive after schedule 149, one on Park Drive after schedule 150 - and **neither carries a number**, so neither can go into the unoccupied list without inventing an address. Left unrecorded rather than guessed.

**Charles Loder** at schedule 160, coachman, born Compton in Berkshire with a wife born at Lydd in Kent, is the Huntingdon Drive man the 1911 round records as born “near Ashford” - the Kent birth in 1911 is his wife's county, not his.

**Parker Woodward** at schedule 158 is now a solicitor at 36, with five children. The 1871 round has him an articled clerk.
